title: Personal Credit Cards: points left on a card that is being closed
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: counting the points left on a card at closing

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When a cardholder who is closing a card asks to cash out its rewards points, it fixes how many points are left on the card to be cashed out.

## Rule

The points left on the card are counted from the card's ledger at handling time, as:

1. the total of all points posted by the card's earning entries,
2. less the total of all points posted by the card's redemption entries,
3. less the total of all points posted by the card's forfeiture entries, including removals that take back the points of a refunded purchase.

## Worked example (hypothetical ledger at closing)

| Ledger entries on the card | Points |
|---|---|
| earning entries | 9800 |
| redemption entries | 2500 |
| forfeiture entries | 700 |
| points left on the card | 9800 less 2500 less 700, that is 6600 |

## Points of judgement

- The count includes every entry of each kind on this card's ledger, from opening to handling time.
- Points on another card of the same cardholder are not part of the count.
- The figure is the ledger count itself; a points figure taken from elsewhere does not replace it.
